corrections.source_says: Set to met. The school was selected by convenience, but class names were drawn from a bag: the first class drawn received the ChatGPT intervention and the next became the control. This is random assignment through classes, consistent with the existing field_rct design classification, and warrants the two-screener pipeline despite the author calling the design quasi-experimental.

corrections.source_says: Set to yes under the supplied codebook: class-level random assignment, 60 analyzed people (30 per arm), and researcher-scored creative writing outputs satisfy all three criteria. Update the reason accordingly. One class per arm, post-assignment exclusions, bundled feedback and instruction, and participant-level tests without a reported class-adjusted analysis remain methodological limitations; they do not make the stated eligibility criteria unclear. Core eligibility does not establish suitability of the reported precision for pooling.
corrections.quote: Araştırmanın çalışma grubu, Van ilinde devlet okullarının birinde 3. sınıfta öğrenimine devam eden 60 öğrenciden oluşmaktadır.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 8 (Sayfa 77), Çalışma grubu and Tablo 1; PDF p. 11 (Sayfa 80), exclusions and scoring; PDF p. 15 (Sayfa 84), Tablo 6. Eligibility and pooling are distinguished in creativity-codebook.md, sections 3 and 10.

corrections.form_value: Pre-test and post-test stories: one lesson hour (40 minutes) each. Intervention: 3 lesson hours (40+40+40 minutes) one day a week for 6 weeks (weeks 2-7); 8 weeks in total.
corrections.source_says: The pre-test is explicitly allotted one lesson hour (40 minutes). The subsequent paragraph describes the post-test but gives no duration, so its duration should be not_stated (or null), rather than 40 minutes. The intervention duration of 3 lesson hours (40+40+40 minutes), one day per week for 6 weeks, and 8 weeks overall is supported.

confirmed: Source: the complete 24-page journal PDF, Batı Anadolu Eğitim Bilimleri Dergisi 17(1), 70-93, DOI 10.51460/baebd.1757062; received 2 August 2025, accepted 16 January 2026, published 28 April 2026. The bilingual title and sole author Emrah Kultas match the form (PDF p. 1, Sayfa 70; PDF page count).

All markdown was read, including references and appendices. Ek 1 contains intervention-week student texts, Ek 2 post-test-week student texts, and Ek 3 ChatGPT examples; the appendices contain no statistical tables (PDF pp. 22-24, Sayfa 91-93, text and page images).

One substantive outcome study assigns two intact third-grade classes by lottery from eight sections in one public school in Van; one class per arm. field_rct, assignment unit class, and context_class none are supported under the codebook (PDF p. 8, Sayfa 77, Çalışma grubu; PDF p. 14, Sayfa 83, Geçerlik ve güvenirlik).

The analyzed sample is 60 children, 30 per arm, not texts, ratings, or clusters; it is not below the 50-person threshold. Experimental: 18 girls and 12 boys; control: 14 girls and 16 boys; school year 2024-2025 (PDF p. 2, Sayfa 71, abstracts; PDF p. 8, Sayfa 77, Tablo 1; PDF p. 15, Sayfa 84, Tablo 6).

Following class assignment and preliminary free writing, data from 4 experimental and 5 control students with low writing skills were excluded. People counts at randomization are not explicitly reported, so the null randomized counts are appropriate (PDF pp. 10-11, Sayfa 79-80, Veri toplama süreci).

The separate pilot class was used to assess activity feasibility and time requirements; no participant count or scored creativity result is reported for that pilot (PDF p. 11, Sayfa 80, first paragraph).

The intervention used GPT-3.5 through the OpenAI webpage, mediated by the teacher on the classroom electronic board. Students compared same-topic AI examples with their own writing and revised it; they did not individually use ChatGPT (PDF p. 9, Sayfa 78, ChatGPT; PDF p. 12, Sayfa 81, intervention procedure).

The schedule is pre-test in week 1, intervention in weeks 2-7, and post-test in week 8. ChatGPT is listed only during intervention, supporting after_ai and a later-session outcome; elapsed days are not specified (PDF p. 12, Sayfa 81, Tablo 4; PDF p. 11, Sayfa 80, post-test paragraph).
Tablo 3 specifies pre-test words Vatan, bayrak, asker, arkadaşlık, köy and post-test words Bütçe, aile, alışveriş, ihtiyaç, istek, yardım (PDF p. 10, Sayfa 79, Tablo 3).

The researcher scored student texts with Kasap (2019): a one-dimensional 24-item scale, 1-5 per item, total range 24-120, sample Cronbach alpha .88. This is an output-scored overall-creativity outcome, with one post-test score per analyzed participant (PDF p. 8, Sayfa 77, Veri toplama araçları; PDF p. 11, Sayfa 80, scoring procedure).

Performance bands are low 24-48, medium 49-72, good 73-96, advanced 97-120; post-test counts are experimental 7 low, 6 medium, 12 good, 5 advanced, and control 25 low, 5 medium (PDF p. 9, Sayfa 78, Tablo 2; PDF p. 15, Sayfa 84, paragraph between Tables 6 and 7).
Tablo 6 pre-test: Deney N 30, mean 34,23, S 14,56; Kontrol N 30, mean 35,66, S 10,82; sd 58, t -.433, p .667. Every corresponding number in the reported string matches (PDF p. 15, Sayfa 84, Tablo 6).
Tablo 6 post-test: Deney N 30, mean 73,40, S 24,61; Kontrol N 30, mean 40,23, S 11,33; sd 58, t 6.705, p .000. The one-line finding reproduces these values correctly (PDF p. 15, Sayfa 84, Tablo 6).

Tablo 7 prints experimental t -7.887 and control t -8.238, with sd 29 and p .000 for both; it prints control post-test S 11,31, whereas Tablo 6 prints 11,33. The form correctly preserves that discrepancy and uses the table degrees of freedom, although accompanying prose uses t(30) and the table heading says Shapiro-Wilk (PDF p. 15, Sayfa 84, Tables 6-7; PDF p. 16, Sayfa 85, first paragraph).

Tablo 8 reports post-test eta .771 and eta-squared .594, as recorded in both the reported string and one-line finding. These are the printed effect-size statistics, not a pooled estimate or a reported standardized mean difference (PDF p. 16, Sayfa 85, Tablo 8).

The treatment bundles AI examples with peer/teacher feedback, creative-writing instruction, and rewriting; the control receives no teacher feedback. The author explicitly says the gain cannot be separated into a ChatGPT effect versus feedback in general (PDF p. 9, Sayfa 78, ChatGPT; PDF pp. 12-13, Sayfa 81-82, procedure; PDF p. 16, Sayfa 85, discussion).

This is an original people study, not a synthesis or AI-versus-human-output comparison; no between-person diversity outcome or synthesis estimates are reported (PDF p. 7, Sayfa 76, research questions and design; PDF pp. 15-16, Sayfa 84-85, results).
summary: Class-level lottery assignment and 60 analyzed students establish a randomized people study meeting the core criteria. Reported statistics match the PDF; correct the two eligibility fields and remove the unsupported 40-minute post-test duration.
